cur:monumental-san-blind-men-jericho.summary: Christ, haloed and in purple, reaches out to touch the eyes of a blind man with a staff, while a second blind man stands beside him and an apostle in white follows behind. The figures stand on a strip of green ground against the gold, framed by the jewelled border common to the whole cycle. The scene presents Christ as the light-giver who opens the eyes of those who call to him.
facts: The thirteen scenes of the north wall show Christ's miracles and teaching; in all of them he appears young and beardless, robed in imperial purple.
The scenes were not arranged in biblical order but are thought to follow the Gospel readings of the Lenten liturgy in Theodoric's palace church.

cur:monumental-porec-arch-christ-apostle.summary: Across the wall above the apse arch, Christ sits enthroned on a blue globe at the centre, holding an open book, flanked by the twelve apostles who stand in white against the gold, six on each side, each with his attribute. Below, a ring of medallions on the arch holds the Lamb of God and twelve female martyrs, and in the apse the Virgin and Child are enthroned among angels and saints.
facts: Christ's open book carries the words EGO SUM LUX VERA, 'I am the true light'.
The basilica was built from 553 under Bishop Euphrasius, with wall mosaics by Byzantine masters; it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.

cur:objects-coin-constantine-vii-zoe-sol.summary: On the obverse Christ Pantokrator sits on a throne with a curved back, blessing and holding the Gospels, within the legend 'Jesus Christ, King of those who reign'. The reverse shows the boy emperor Constantine VII and his mother, the empress Zoe Karbonopsina, holding a patriarchal cross between them. The enthroned Christ assures the legitimacy of a child ruler under his mother's regency.
facts: Zoe Karbonopsina, fourth wife of Leo VI, served as regent for her son Constantine VII from 913 until 919, when Romanos Lekapenos seized power (Wikipedia).
The CNG catalogue dates this specimen precisely to 6 February 914.
